title: Longest Stable Sensor Window
summary: Find the longest run of sensor readings whose spread stays within a tolerance.

stages.title: Longest stable window
stages.requirement:
A temperature sensor emits integer readings. A window is **stable** if
`max(window) - min(window) <= tolerance`. Write `longest_stable_window(readings, tolerance)`
returning the length of the longest stable **contiguous** window. Return 0 for no readings.
`tolerance >= 0`.

```python
longest_stable_window([8, 2, 4, 7], 4)          # -> 2   ([2, 4] or [4, 7])
longest_stable_window([10, 1, 2, 4, 7, 2], 5)   # -> 4   ([2, 4, 7, 2])
```

Up to 100,000 readings.

hiddenTests.name: test_large_monotonic
hiddenTests.description: A window that re-scans for min/max each step is too slow here.

hiddenTests.name: test_large_against_brute_force

hints: If a window is unstable, any window containing it is unstable too, so a two-pointer sliding window works.
The hard part is knowing the current window's min and max in O(1) as both ends move.
Keep two monotonic deques of indices: one decreasing (front is the max), one increasing (front is the min). Pop fronts that fall out of the window.

solution.explanation:
Stability is monotone: shrinking a window never makes it unstable. That allows a sliding
window where `right` advances every step and `left` only moves forward. Two monotonic
deques keep the window max and min at their fronts. Each index is pushed and popped at
most once per deque, so the whole pass is linear.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) worst case for the deques
